q: Most of the metals are ____ at room temperature, and therefore, there must be some sort of bonding between these metal atoms.
e: The strength of metallic bonding keeps most metals in a solid crystalline state at room temperature.

q: These metal atoms are held together in solid ____ form by a metallic bonding.
e: Metals adopt highly ordered, closely packed crystalline lattice structures.

q: In a metallic bond, the atoms do not share or ____ electrons to bond together.
e: Unlike ionic or covalent bonds, metallic bonding involves delocalized electrons rather than fixed sharing or transfer.

q: The structure of a metallic bond is quite ____ from that of covalent or ionic bonds.
e: The electron sea model fundamentally distinguishes metallic bonding from localized bond types.

q: In ____ solids, e.g., sodium, magnesium, and aluminium, atoms of metals are present.
e: Metallic solids consist entirely of metal atoms held together by metallic bonds.

q: In a metallic bond, the valence electrons of the atoms are very ____ held, forming a common electron cloud.
e: Low ionization energies allow valence electrons to detach from individual atoms.

q: These valence electrons move ____ within this electron cloud.
e: The delocalized electrons are not bound to any specific nucleus and can drift through the lattice.

q: These mobile electrons are often described as "a ____ of electrons" which make the metals easily conduct electricity.
e: The electron sea model visualizes valence electrons as a fluid surrounding positive metal cores.

q: The ____ charged metallic nuclei are surrounded by free-moving electrons.
e: After losing valence electrons, the metal atoms become positively charged cations.

q: The bonding results from the ____ of these electrons with the various nuclei.
e: The continuous electrostatic interaction between the electron sea and cations holds the metal together.

q: Hence, they are held together by a strong ____ attraction that results in low volatility of the metals.
e: Electrostatic forces between the sea of electrons and positive ions prevent metals from easily vaporizing.

q: Metals consist of giant structures of atoms that are packed closely together in a regular arrangement called a ____.
e: Metal atoms pack efficiently into regular geometric lattices to maximize bonding interactions.

q: The strength of metallic bonding increases with (1) the increasing ____ charge on the ions in the metal lattice.
e: Higher ionic charge increases the electrostatic pull on the delocalized electron sea.

q: ...(2) the ____ size of metal ions in the lattice.
e: Smaller ions allow the positive nuclei to get closer to the electron sea, strengthening the bond.

q: ...and (3) the increasing number of ____ electrons (valence electrons) per atom.
e: More delocalized electrons per atom create a denser, more strongly binding electron sea.

q: However, the strength of metallic bond is ____ than that of an ionic bond.
e: Generally, the rigid electrostatic lattice of ionic compounds is stronger than the flexible metallic bond.

q: Consequently, the melting points of some metals become ____ compared with the ionic compounds.
e: Weaker overall bonding means less thermal energy is required to disrupt the metallic lattice.
